Q: Send Mail from Windows Machine using Shell ( from Git bash) A:

Git Bash on Windows does not include /usr/sbin/sendmail. It provides Unix-like command-line tools, but it is not a complete Linux installation. Since the updated question already uses PowerShell, invoke a PowerShell script from Git Bash and send the HTML body with -BodyAsHtml.

Read the file as one string:

$body = Get-Content -Path "C:\Users\xyz\Documents\failed_cloud_alert\missJobMailer.txt" -Raw

Send-MailMessage `
    -To "recipient@example.com" `
    -From "sender@example.com" `
    -Subject "TEST" `
    -Body $body `
    -BodyAsHtml `
    -SmtpServer "smtp.example.com"

Without -BodyAsHtml, PowerShell sends the body as text/plain, so the recipient sees the HTML source. The file must also contain valid HTML.

From Git Bash, run the saved script with:

powershell.exe -NoProfile -File "C:\path\to\send-alert.ps1"

You still need the SMTP host, port, TLS and authentication settings required by the mail service. Those settings come from the mail provider or system administrator; Windows cannot reliably discover arbitrary SMTP credentials automatically.

For new code, note that Send-MailMessage is obsolete. A maintained SMTP library such as MailKit is a better long-term choice.

Q: PostgreSQL rename table - cascade renaming to objects like indices, constraints that contain table name A:

This will rename any index which name not following $tableName_$columnName(composite index will concat each name of column component with _), primary key index for $tableName_pkey and other rules for constraint name: PostgreSQL: default constraint names, note it's possible to override the default rule when CREATE TABLE: PostgreSQL: is it possible to provide custom name for PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE?

-- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65069778/postgresql-rename-table-cascade-renaming-to-objects-like-indices-constraints/78485773#78485773
DO
$do$
DECLARE
    r record;
    target_schema text := 'your_schema';
BEGIN
    FOR r IN
        WITH table_indexes AS (
            SELECT ct.relname "table", ci.relname "index", c.contype constraint_type, a.attname "column"
            FROM pg_index i -- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37329561/how-to-list-indexes-created-for-table-in-postgres/37330092#37330092
            JOIN pg_class ct ON ct.oid = i.indrelid
            JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = ct.relnamespace
            JOIN pg_class ci ON ci.oid = i.indexrelid
            JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = i.indrelid AND a.attnum = ANY(i.indkey) AND a.attnum > 0 -- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/55447819/how-to-get-the-list-of-column-names-for-all-indexes-on-a-table-in-postgresql/55448707#55448707
            LEFT JOIN pg_constraint c ON c.conindid = i.indexrelid -- https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/catalog-pg-constraint.html
            WHERE n.nspname = target_schema
        ), table_index_names AS (
            SELECT "table", "index",
                   format('%s%s_%s',
                          "table",
                          CASE constraint_type
                              -- only uncomment below line when using postgresql<12 https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4107915/postgresql-default-constraint-names#comment109084417_4108266
                              -- WHEN 'f' THEN '_' || "column"[1] -- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4107915/postgresql-default-constraint-names#comment127573826_4108266
                              WHEN 'p' THEN '' -- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4107915/postgresql-default-constraint-names#comment127553786_4108266
                              ELSE '_' || string_agg("column", '_')
                          END,
                          CASE coalesce(constraint_type, 'NULL') -- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/15417167/case-when-null-evaluates-to-false
                              -- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4107915/postgresql-default-constraint-names/4108266#4108266
                              -- https://gist.github.com/popravich/d6816ef1653329fb1745
                              -- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/8674562/postgresql-is-it-possible-to-provide-custom-name-for-primary-key-or-unique/8674640#8674640
                              WHEN 'c' THEN 'check'
                              WHEN 'f' THEN 'fkey'
                              WHEN 'p' THEN 'pkey'
                              WHEN 'u' THEN 'key'
                              WHEN 'x' THEN 'excl'
                              WHEN 'NULL' THEN 'idx'
                          END
                   ) new_index
            FROM table_indexes
            GROUP BY "table", "index", constraint_type
        )
        SELECT format('ALTER INDEX %I RENAME TO %I', "index", new_index) sql, *
        FROM table_index_names
        WHERE "index" != new_index
    LOOP
        -- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1348126/postgresql-modify-owner-on-all-tables-simultaneously-in-postgresql/37259655#37259655
        RAISE NOTICE '%', r.sql; -- dry-run
        -- EXECUTE r.sql; -- uncomment to run them
        COMMIT; -- https://dba.stackexchange.com/questions/315063/disable-toast-compression-for-all-columns/315067#315067
    END LOOP;
END
$do$

Q: Error:MetaGraphDef associated with tags 'serve' could not be found in SavedModel A:

You seem to have what is called a frozen graph. Those cannot be converted, nor do they have a graph definition. See this discussion for a detailed answer.

For comparison with a saved model (with graph definition) where a conversion works, see this hello_world example from Tensorflow Lite Micro. When you either train the model yourself based on the provided Jupyter notebook or download the hello_world.zip you get saved_model.pb. Enter the directory where this file is located, models/model and type

saved_model_cli show --dir ./ --all

then you get a long list of information. Or either

saved_model_cli show --dir=./

you get

The given SavedModel contains the following tag-sets: 'serve'
